# OpenAI API error: "The model `text-davinci-003` has been deprecated"

You are encountering a specific deprecation notice because OpenAI has officially sunset the legacy completion models, including `text-davinci-003`. The error message you received is unambiguous: `{ "error": { "message": "The model `text-davinci-003` has been deprecated...", "code": "model_not_found" } }`. This isn't a temporary outage or a configuration mismatch on your end; the endpoint simply no longer exists.

The code snippet you were likely provided, `$endpoint = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/engines/text-davinci-003/completions';`, relies on the older v1 Completions API architecture. While this was the standard for years, it has been deprecated in favor of the Chat Completions API. Continuing to use the old endpoint will result in a `404 Not Found` or a deprecation error every time you make a request.

To resolve this, you must migrate your codebase to the new `chat/completions` endpoint and switch to a supported model like `gpt-3.5-turbo` or `gpt-4`. The API response format changes slightly between these two architectures, so a simple URL swap is not enough; you often need to adjust how you structure your payloads.

### Migrating the Endpoint

The first step is updating your endpoint URL. Replace the legacy engine path with the new chat completions path:

```php
$endpoint = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions';
```

This change alone will stop the `model_not_found` error from throwing immediately, but you must also update the model name in your request body. You can no longer pass `text-davinci-003`. Instead, you should use:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-3.5-turbo",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Your prompt here"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Handling Payload Differences

The most significant friction point during migration is the payload structure. The legacy Completions API expected a `prompt` field containing a string of text. The new Chat API expects an array of objects under the `messages` key, where each object defines a role (`system`, `assistant`, or `user`) and content.

If your application currently sends a single prompt string to `text-davinci-003`, you cannot simply map that directly without modification. You must wrap your input in a message object:

```php
$data = [
    'model' => 'gpt-3.5-turbo',
    'messages' => [
        [
            'role' => 'user',
            'content' => $yourOriginalPromptString
        ]
    ],
    'temperature' => 0.7
];
```

### Trade-offs and Considerations

Migrating to the Chat API offers more than just fixing an error code. The new architecture provides better context handling, allowing you to maintain conversation history across multiple turns rather than treating every request as an isolated interaction. This is particularly useful for chatbots or multi-step reasoning tasks.

However, there are trade-offs to consider. The Chat API can be slightly more expensive per token depending on the model you choose (`gpt-4` vs `gpt-3.5-turbo`). Additionally, the response structure changes; instead of receiving a raw completion string directly in the top-level JSON, it is nested within a `choices[0].message.content` array. You will need to update your parsing logic accordingly.

If you are maintaining legacy integrations that strictly require the old `text-davinci-003` behavior, note that OpenAI has explicitly stated this model is no longer available for new deployments. Attempting to force it via URL manipulation or version hacking will not work and will only result in continued errors.

For developers looking for robust, well-documented integrations with these modern APIs, resources like [https://laravelcompany.com](https://laravelcompany.com) often provide useful patterns for handling API versions and migrations within the Laravel ecosystem. Ensuring your application is built on the latest stable endpoints prevents technical debt before it becomes a migration nightmare later on.

The transition requires updating both your URL and your request payload structure, but it unlocks access to the full capabilities of the current OpenAI models.
